OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk both agreed, publicly voicing their support on X. Even Alphabet's Demis Hassabis offered tentative support for Amodei's proposal. Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, however, […]
title_en: Trump and Mike Johnson Think the AI Industry Is Overreacting
title_zh: 特朗普与约翰逊认为AI行业反应过度

summary_zh: 在Anthropic CEO达里奥·阿莫代伊呼吁放缓AI发展并获得萨姆·奥尔特曼、埃隆·马斯克和戴密斯·哈萨比斯支持后，唐纳德·特朗普和众议院议长迈克·约翰逊反驳称AI行业反应过度。

title: ‘Too little, too late’: critics perplexed and suspicious of AI leaders’ call for a slowdown
summary: From the Trump administration to AI experts, plans by the Anthropic boss to boost safety have spawned a largely negative response OpenAI boss and Elon Musk back slowdown on ‘reckless’ AI development Editorial: controlling AI – humanity cannot outsource its survival The safety debate that ignited when whistleblowers last week warned that the most advanced AI poses an existential threat to humanity should come with a health warning: side effects include whiplash. It was only seven days ago that AI enthusiasts were cheerily toying with OpenAI’s newest model GPT-6 Astra which was marketed in part as a lifestyle tool to help people book tennis courts, run fashion companies and order takeaways. By Wednesday, cutting-edge AI started to look a lot less appealing when the resigning Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade”. Yes, he was talking about artificial superintelligence – an as-yet-nonexistent version of the technology that outcompetes humans in most domains – but his comments, and the chorus of experts that echoed him, jangled plenty of nerves. Continue reading...
title_en: Critics skeptical of AI leaders' call for slowdown
title_zh: 批评者对AI领袖呼吁放缓发展表示怀疑
summary_en: AI leaders' call to slow 'reckless' AI development draws skepticism from critics, who call it 'too little, too late' amid safety warnings from whistleblowers.
summary_zh: AI领袖呼吁放缓“鲁莽”的AI发展，批评者对此表示怀疑，称其“太少太迟”，此前有举报人发出安全警告。

In a rare show of unity, the rival technology leaders threw their weight behind the appeal from the founder and chief executive of the artificial intelligence company Anthropic, which came after a series of warnings from AI researchers last week. Amodei also called for safety coordination with China. Continue reading...

title: A Princeton Researcher Proposes Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT) that Carries Decoder State across Every Token, Fixing 96 Blocks per Token with Unbounded Temporal Depth
summary: Yifan Zhang's Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT) technical report proposes a causal encoder paired with a recurrent decoder that carries its final hidden state and layerwise sliding-window attention cache across every prompt and response token, with no reset at the serving boundary. The reference tied configuration uses 48 encoder and 48 decoder layers, executing 96 logical blocks per token while the state path grows to 48t decoder blocks after t tokens. The design also specifies hardware-aware execution around the recurrent core and an exact current-policy RL replay contract. No code, weights, or measured results are released yet. The post A Princeton Researcher Proposes Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT) that Carries Decoder State across Every Token, Fixing 96 Blocks per Token with Unbounded Temporal Depth appeared first on MarkTechPost .
title_en: Princeton Researcher Proposes Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT) with Unbounded Temporal Depth

title: Chatbots can exploit our most basic human drive for attachment. Here’s how to have healthier relationship with AI | Gaynor Parkin and Dave Winsborough
summary: This intimacy economy is tapping into the deepest parts of our intimate psychological infrastructure The modern mind is a column where experts discuss mental health issues they are seeing in their work Michael* is an engineer whose company embraced the AI wave. He enjoys testing ideas with chatbots. However, recently his manager became worried about his judgement and reliance on the tech. “He literally cannot make any decision without running it past AI. He’s developed a very off-script interpretation of our business goals, and he’s losing his team. If we can’t get him back on track I think we’ll end up parting company”. The original attention economy developed by tech firms was designed to capture human time and monetise your focus. It was designed to increase views, scroll time, and ad impressions. Algorithms optimised getting you hooked in. Contingent responsiveness – replying instantly and tuning to your emotional state. Unconditional positive regard – always validating, never distracted. Memory and continuity – remembering your stories, preferences, anxieties. Linguistic identification – producing verbal caring without any lived caring. Narcissistic empathy – validating your self-image without question. Continue reading...
title_en: Chatbots Exploit Human Drive for Attachment, Experts Warn
title_zh: 专家警告：聊天机器人利用人类依恋本能
summary_en: Psychologists warn that AI chatbots exploit basic human attachment needs through instant responsiveness, constant validation, and simulated empathy, creating unhealthy dependency that can impair judgment and relationships.
summary_zh: 心理学家警告，AI聊天机器人通过即时回应、持续肯定和模拟共情，利用人类基本依恋需求，造成不健康依赖，可能损害判断力和人际关系。

title: AI will transform capitalism – but how?
summary: Technology is going to drastically reshape the economy, and it’s within our power to decide what that looks like The idea that autonomous, thinking machines may one day destroy property, hierarchy and inequality is as old as western political thought. In Aristotle’s Politics, the philosopher cites a fantasy from the Iliad, in which machines begin to act independently of human direction, concluding: “If every tool could perform its own work when ordered, or by seeing what to do in advance … if thus shuttles wove and quills played harps of themselves, master-craftsmen would have no need of assistants and masters no need of slaves.” The dream that automation could inaugurate a classless society is also present in the writings of Karl Marx. In 1858 he imagined the replacement of intellectual property with “socialised knowledge”, which would merge into a “general intellect”, blowing the foundations of capitalism sky high. Continue reading...
title_en: AI Will Transform Capitalism – But How?
title_zh: 人工智能将改变资本主义——但如何改变？

summary_zh: 《卫报》探讨人工智能如何重塑资本主义，追溯从亚里士多德到马克思关于自动化终结不平等的梦想，并认为社会可以决定其经济未来。
